title: Veggie Egg Burritos
subtitle: Big-batch burritos that hold on the line and reheat clean.
description: Breakfast at the station has to survive interruptions. This recipe is written for real timing, clear heat cues, and a workflow that keeps food hot while the board gets loud.

ingredients.name: large eggs
ingredients.notes: whisked with a pinch of salt

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Veggie Egg Burritos in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Crisp the potatoes
steps.instruction: Heat a large skillet or griddle over medium-high. Add hash browns in an even layer; press with a spatula. Let them sit until browned, flip in sections, and season with salt and pepper. Move to a warm tray. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale.

steps.title: Brown the meat + veg
steps.instruction: In the same pan, brown sausage/chorizo. Add onion and peppers; cook until softened. Drain excess fat if needed so burritos don’t get greasy. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Soft-scramble the eggs
steps.instruction: Lower heat to medium. Add a touch of butter, then the eggs. Stir gently until just set (slightly glossy). Fold in cheese off heat so it melts without overcooking. Plan about 6 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build and wrap for the line
steps.instruction: Warm tortillas briefly. Add potatoes, meat/veg, eggs, and a spoon of salsa. Roll tight: fold sides, then roll forward. Hold wrapped burritos seam-side down on a warm sheet pan. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Serve + hold
steps.instruction: Keep burritos warm in a 200°F oven (uncovered for crispy tortillas; covered for softer). If you’re feeding in waves, build half, serve, then build the rest. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Assign one cook to the hot surface and one to assembly. Keep the line moving; don’t crowd the griddle.
Set a warm holding zone (oven 200°F or covered hotel pan) so staggered eaters still get a hot plate.
Run a quick call-proof check: anything crispy stays uncovered; anything soft stays covered.
cleanupNotes: While plates are served, scrape the griddle/pan and wipe with a damp towel (use tongs + folded towel).
Soak the mixing bowl and sheet pan immediately—breakfast starch sets fast when it cools.
leftovers: Cool fast: spread on a sheet pan 10 minutes, then portion into containers so it doesn’t sweat.
Reheat rule: eggs reheat best covered at 50% power or low oven heat; don’t nuke on high.
